Create a standards schema

Source: R/standards.R
standards_schema.Rd

Standardizes a standards lookup table for use with environmental chemistry analyses.

standards_schema(
  data,
  analyte,
  standard_value,
  standard_unit,
  standard_type,
  location = NULL,
  medium = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  provenance = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  effective_date = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  priority = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing standards information.

analyte

Column containing analyte names.

standard_value

Column containing standard values.

standard_unit

Column containing standard units.

standard_type

Column containing standard categories or criterion names.

location

Optional column containing location-specific standards.

medium

Optional column containing medium information.

source

Optional column containing source organization or authority.

provenance

Optional column containing regulation, program, permit, guidance document, or project identifier.

reference

Optional citation, URL, permit number, regulation citation, or other reference.

effective_date

Optional effective date.

notes

Optional comments.

priority

Optional numeric priority used to resolve conflicts when multiple standards match the same observation. Lower values indicate higher precedence.

Value

A tibble with class "standards_schema" containing the following standardized columns:

.analyte

Analyte name.

.standard_type

Standard category or criterion name.

.standard_value

Numeric standard value.

.standard_unit

Unit associated with the standard.

.location

Optional location identifier.

.medium

Environmental medium.

.source

Source authority or organization.

.provenance

Regulation, permit, program, or guidance source.

.reference

Reference citation or URL.

.effective_date

Effective date of the standard.

.notes

Additional comments.

.priority

Conflict-resolution priority. Lower values take precedence over higher values.

Details

This constructor converts a user-supplied standards table into a validated standards_schema object that can be used by [assign_standards()].

Standards may represent regulatory criteria, permit limits, screening levels, background concentrations, or project-specific objectives. Optional metadata may be included to document the source, applicability, and provenance of each standard.

The .priority field determines which standard is selected when multiple standards apply to a single observation.

Lower values represent higher priority.

Recommended priority ranges are:

  • 1-9 = Site- or project-specific objectives

  • 10-19 = Permit limits and compliance criteria

  • 20-49 = Regulatory standards

  • 50-99 = Screening levels and guidance values

  • 100+ = Background or informational values

If priority is not supplied, default priorities are assigned:

  • Location-specific standards receive priority 1

  • All other standards receive priority 100

See also

[assign_standards()], [validate_standards_schema()]
